description: resilience performance/resilience budgets. Never edited by test code — scripts/performance/lib/budget-evaluator.mjs only reads this file and compares measured values against it. baselineValue starts null ("no baseline yet", only absoluteMaximum enforced) and is set only by an explicit operator edit after a real accepted lab.resilience.benchmark/soak run; changing it produces a diff in scripts/performance/generate-resilience-report.mjs output. Security/rate-limit fields (client_max_body_size 64k, 20r/s per-IP, 30r/s ingest per-IP, 200r/s ingest global — infrastructure/docker/reverse-proxy/nginx.conf) are never loosened by any budget here.

budgets.rationale: recordAction() is a synchronous, main-thread call site invoked directly from host application event handlers; it must never be a perceptible source of input lag.
Same synchronous main-thread contract as recordAction; error capture must not add jank on the error path.
security-acceptance closed a sanitizer regex-DoS finding; this is the regression budget that keeps the fix honest under oversized/adversarial payload classes, not just the small-payload common case.
Heap does not need to return to exactly its pre-load value, but a session-scoped SDK must not show unbounded growth across load/recovery cycles.
End-to-end proxy hop latency for a typical RUM/log ingest request under normal load, excluding SDK batch delay.
Normal-profile traffic must never produce an unexpected 5xx; controlled 429 under burst is the only acceptable non-2xx class.
Time from proxy acceptance to first queryable storage visibility for a canary record, measured separately from the ~35s SDK batch delay so it is never conflated with it.

p95 across the full 26-query dashboard-governance manifest catalog against reference-lab fixture data; a single manifest exceeding its own timeoutBudgetMs is a hard failure independent of this aggregate.
Bounded time from openobserve/alert-sink becoming healthy again to the first successful readiness-probe notification; not a guaranteed-delivery claim, only a recovery-time bound.
OpenObserve is the heaviest container (2 CPU / 3G limit); this bounds cold-restart readiness on the reference lab.
nginx is lightweight; a slow proxy restart would point at a real regression, not normal variance.
Node http-test-service image cold start is fast; also exercises the new depends_on.restart:true auto-recovery wiring.
Peak RSS/deploy.resources.limits.memory ratio must stay clear of the OOM boundary under burst, per-service.

Open file descriptor count is not expected to return exactly to baseline after a load/recovery cycle, but a large, monotonic per-cycle delta is an early leak signal worth tracking even before it becomes a hard failure.
